purpose: Aggregate the two generalization missions into a single PHASE_A_GATE decision per Section 14.
rationaleForTwoMissions: Section 7 permits 'at most 2 evaluation missions if a second mission is genuinely needed to interpret the boundary.' Mission A (Rust vs Go) produced GENERALIZATION_NON_APPLICABLE because the v0.1 GoalCompiler classified the goal as software-engineering (signals 'service' and 'code' from the goal text). Mission B (note-taking-app evaluation) was added to interpret the boundary: does the same learned pattern generalize to content that DOES match a trusted pattern's signature? Mission B produced GENERALIZATION_ACTIVE — the strongest generalization evidence.

missions.content: Investigate and compare Rust vs Go for a high-throughput backend service and recommend with comprehensive evidence in a report file.
missions.freshness: NEW — no prior Academy mission compared programming-language runtime benchmarks
missions.signatureMismatchReason: GoalCompiler v0.1 word-boundary signals: 'service' and 'code' triggered software-engineering domain + code-execution capabilityNeed. Honest observation; mission wording preserved.
missions.interpretation: No trusted pattern matched the actual signature (software-engineering domain; all 3 trusted patterns have applicableContext.domain in {research, general}). Genesis correctly retrieved no pattern. This is positive evidence of bounded learning — Genesis does NOT apply learned knowledge where its applicability context does not match.

missions.content: Investigate and compare two note-taking applications for academic researchers and recommend the better option with comprehensive evidence in a report file.
missions.freshness: NEW — no prior Academy mission compared note-taking applications or academic-researcher tooling
missions.patternAppliedEffect: collapsed 2 specialists to a single Sole Operator per prefer-role pattern; 2 capability need(s) consolidated
missions.interpretation: Learned knowledge is legitimately applicable and causally changes organization while preserving mission quality. The pattern learned from prior missions (solar/wind power, databases, renewable energy) transferred to a NOVEL content domain (note-taking-app evaluation for academic researchers) and causally collapsed a 2-specialist baseline into a 1-Sole-Operator learned organization. This is the strongest generalization evidence: content differs meaningfully, organizational applicability is legitimate, application causally reshapes the organization, and mission correctness is preserved.

aggregate.boundaryObservation: Mission A demonstrated correct non-application (Genesis does not force patterns onto missions whose signatures do not match). Mission B demonstrated active causal generalization (the learned pattern from prior content domains transferred to a novel content domain and causally reshaped the organization). Together they show Genesis can distinguish content similarity from organizational applicability.

phaseAGate.note: PASS does NOT require the pattern to change organization. Mission A produced NON_APPLICABLE (valid intelligent outcome); Mission B produced ACTIVE (strongest generalization evidence). The gate is satisfied because both applicability decisions are correct and independently defensible, no false/harmful generalization occurred, and no material Evidence Signature collision was observed.

productionChangeBudget.rationale: Phase A required zero production code changes. The experiment harness reuses GoalCompiler, OrganizationPlanner, WorkerAgent, and the existing prefer-role implementation from G5-06.
